newsitem.title: QATAR: Unified Gulf Arab tariffs within 2-3 years - GCC.
newsitem.headline: Unified Gulf Arab tariffs within 2-3 years - GCC.

text.p: Gulf Arab states said on Monday they needed another two to three years to unify custom tariffs, a key condition by other major trading groups for forging a free trade accord with the oil-rich alliance.

"A modality has been placed...An accord was reached that within two years or three at the most there will be committees which have reached agreement on the Gulf customs tariff unity," said Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani.

The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) on Monday ended its annual summit in Qatar, the group's new rotating chairman over the next year. Bahrain boycotted this year's event but OPEC heavyweights Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait and Qatar along with small oil exporter Oman attended.
EU-GCC talks on forging a free trade accord have been blocked over more than 10 years by the European Union's demand that GCC states should first unify tariffs.

In April the foreign ministers of the two blocs agreed on a time frame of no more than two years to complete the crucial free trade accord which could open European markets for cheap petrochemicals from GCC states.
But differences between some GCC members have for years prevented agreement on the step which is needed for the economic and political alliance to move towards forming a common market.
GCC ministers of finance and economy held several sessions during the summit to try to narrow the differences.

"If we continue like this we will not have an accord before five years," said a delegate after the summit, expressing his country's frustration with slow progress to achieve real integration 16 years after the GCC was formed.

The UAE, a major regional trading and re-export hub, is reluctant to raise its tariffs beyond the four to six percent level which is imposed on most goods while Saudi Arabia, which has tariffs of 20 percent on some items, is in favour of a GCC unified level of 8-12 percent for most goods.

A final GCC accord on tariffs has been postponed several times and some officials were expecting one at the last GCC summit in Oman in December 1995. GCC states control almost 50 percent of the world's proven oil reserves.
